sentences.text: NAGARATHNA, J
We have heard learned counsel for the appellant- State as well as learned counsel for the respondent-accused.

2. By the impugned judgment passed in Criminal Appeal Nos.327 of 2014 and 219 of 2015 dated 28.08.2015, by the High Court of Himachal Pradesh at Shimla it has set aside the judgment and order dated 08.08.2014 and 26.08.2014 rendered by the Court of Sessions, Solan, Himachal Pradesh, in Sessions Trial No.18-S/7 of 2012, whereby the respondent-accused who was charged with and tried for the offence punishable under Section 376 IPC and Section 3(2)(v) of the Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes (Prevention of Atrocities) Act, 1989 (for short, the Act)
and convicted him to undergo sentence of rigorous imprisonment of ten years and to pay a fine of Rs.25,000/- for commission of offence punishable under Section 376 IPC and further to undergo imprisonment for life and to pay a fine of Rs.25,000/- punishable under Section 3(2)(v) of the Act .

entities.text: Criminal Appeal Nos.327 of 2014 and 219 of 2015
entities.label: CASE_NUMBER

entities.text: High Court of Himachal Pradesh at Shimla
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: There has also been a default sentence.
3. The High Court has assigned reasons as to why the Sessions Court was not right in convicting the respondent- accused and sentencing him as above.
The learned counsel for the appellant sought to point out that the reasons assigned by the High Court were not correct and contrary to the evidence on record.
4. Per contra, learned counsel for the respondent-accused supported the impugned judgment and order and contended that the Sessions Court was not right in convicting the respondent.
She further submitted that there is a doubt as to whether the respondent was a minor at the relevant point of time.
In fact, there was a consensual relationship between the parties.
Therefore, the offences alleged against the accused were wholly false.
The High Court has rightly acquitted the respondent.

sentences.text: She further submitted that there is no merit in this appeal.

5. Having heard learned counsel for the respective parties and on perusal of the impugned judgment as well as the judgment of the Sessions Court, we find that the High Court was justified in setting aside the judgment of the Sessions Court and acquitting the respondent herein.
6. In view of the above, these appeals are dismissed.
Pending application(s), if any, shall stand disposed of.
